content: Mallinckrodt Incorporated is a company that supplies pharmaceuticals, chemicals, imaging products, and respiratory equipment. It is based in the St. Louis, Missouri area and was recently acquired by Tyco Healthcare, a division of Tyco International. The company is undergoing further reorganization. One of its divisions, Mallinckrodt Baker, was formed through a merger with a chemical supplier originally founded by John Townshend Baker. Mallinckrodt is the only legal supplier of cocaine in the United States. The company obtains cocaine from a Stepan Company facility located in Maywood, New Jersey, which is the sole entity in the U.S. licensed to import coca leaves. Federal regulations prohibit the importation of certain cocaine-derived drugs, such as Esterom, which necessitates reliance on Mallinckrodt as the supplier. Additionally, Mallinckrodt is one of the U.S. importers of opium sourced from India. The Mallinckrodt General Clinical Research Center benefited from contributions made by Edward Mallinckrodt, Jr., who led the company during the 1940s. A significant legal precedent was established in the case of Mallinckrodt, Inc. v. Medipart, Inc., 976 F.2d 700, 708 (Fed. Cir. 1992). This decision affirmed the right of patent holders to impose restrictions on the use of their products even after the sale. This ruling was later referenced in the case Arizona Cartridge Remanufacturers Association Inc. v. Lexmark International Inc., which upheld the enforceability of end-user licensing agreements included with software products against customers.
